newsitem.title: CANADA: Regulators to continue Canadian 88 probe.
newsitem.headline: Regulators to continue Canadian 88 probe.

text.p: Canadian securities regulators plan to continue an investigation into alleged breaches of securities regulations by Canadian 88 Energy Corp and an affiliated firm, despite Canadian 88 calling off its takeover bid for Morrison Petroleums Ltd, a regulatory official said on Monday.

"We're still looking at the pre-bid purchase of stock -- that was our focus at the start of this," Charles Blakie, director of market standards for the Alberta Securities Commission, said in an phone interview on Monday.
In a surprise move, Canadian 88 this weekend scrapped its C$652-million offer for Morrison prior to a hearing before the ASC and Ontario Securities Commission.
The hearing was expected to determine whether Canadian 88's relationship with associated West Central Capital Corp was adequately disclosed in its offer documents.

It was also to probe into whether all Morrison shareholders should have been entitled to sell shares to Canadian 88 on the same cash terms as afforded West Central, which used money loaned by Canadian 88 to purchase about eight percent of Morrison before the bid was launched.
"There was, as I understand, buying and selling going on for that same period, so we routinely will look at that -- who was doing it and why they were doing it," Blakie said.
He said there was no deadline to reach a decision and the investigation's urgency was lessened in light of Canadian 88 scrapping its offer.
"We'll do it in our usual efficient manner. If we come to any conclusions that there has been a breach, we'll take formal action," he said.
He said the investigation would attempt to determine whether West Central had bought Morrison stock using insider knowledge that a bid was to be launched, a practice called "front-running."
The ASC expects to conduct the continuing investigation in association with the OSC, Blakie said.
